simple.meaning: לֹיָה (lôyâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a wreath.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Kings 7:29. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לֹיָה (H3914) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: לֹיָה (lôyâh) / H3914 is traced through 1 Kings 7:29, 1 Kings 7:30, 1 Kings 7:36 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: and on the panels that were between the ledges were lions, oxen, and cherubim; and on the ledges there was a pedestal above; and beneath the lions and oxen were wreaths of hanging work.

timeline.evidenceText: and on the panels that were between the ledges were lions, oxen, and cherubim; and on the ledges there was a pedestal above; and beneath the lions and oxen were wreaths of hanging work.
Every base had four bronze wheels, and axles of bronze; and the four feet of it had supports. The supports were cast beneath the basin, with wreaths at the side of each.
On the plates of its supports, and on its panels, he engraved cherubim, lions, and palm trees, each in its space, with wreaths all around.

definitions.full: H3914. loyah [ לֹיָה ] noun feminine wreath ? (meaning dubious, compare Sta ZAW iii. 1883, 161 ; possibly = לְוֺיָה ); — plural לֹיוֺת 1Kin 7:29-30 , 36 of carved work on bases of lavers in Solomon's temple.
